questions.question: In which of the following are the songs of Alvar saints compiled?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Divya Prabandham**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Divya Prabandham** is a revered collection of hymns composed by the Alvar saints, who were devotional poets in South India.

• The term "Divya Prabandham" translates to "Sacred Compilation" in Tamil, emphasizing its spiritual significance.

• This compilation includes **4,000 hymns** (Naalayira Divya Prabandham) written in Tamil, celebrating the glory of Lord Vishnu and his various forms.

• The Alvar saints were twelve prominent Vaishnavite saints who lived between the **6th and 9th centuries CE** and expressed their devotion through poetry.

• The hymns in the Divya Prabandham cover themes like **bhakti (devotion), surrender, and divine love**, making it a cornerstone of Tamil Vaishnavism.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Ettutogai:** 

• Ettutogai is a collection of classical Tamil literary works belonging to the Sangam period (circa 300 BCE–300 CE).

• It consists of eight anthologies, including works like **Ahananuru, Purananuru, Kuruntokai**, and others, focusing on themes of love and war.

• It is not related to Vaishnavite devotional literature but reflects the socio-cultural aspects of ancient Tamil society.

• **Tipitaka:** 

• Tipitaka, meaning "Three Baskets," is the sacred scripture of Buddhism, written in the Pali language.

• It comprises three parts: **Vinaya Pitaka** (disciplinary rules), **Sutta Pitaka** (teachings of Buddha), and **Abhidhamma Pitaka** (philosophical analysis).

• It is entirely distinct from the Vaishnavite tradition of the Alvar saints.

• **Adi-Puran:** 

• Adi-Puran is a Jain scripture written by Jinasena, focusing on the life stories of Rishabhdev, the first Tirthankara.

• It delves into Jain philosophy and ethics, making it unrelated to the hymns of the Alvar saints.

• **Divya Prabandham:** 

• The Divya Prabandham is central to the Tamil Vaishnavite tradition and is recited in temples during rituals and festivals.

• It forms the basis for the liturgical practices in many Vaishnavite temples, including **Sri Rangam**, one of the most famous temples dedicated to Lord Vishnu.

• The hymns are still preserved and celebrated for their linguistic beauty and spiritual depth, showcasing the cultural richness of Tamil Nadu.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Compilation:** The Divya Prabandham is considered a divine revelation and was compiled by **Nathamuni**, a Vaishnavite scholar, in the 9th century CE.

• **Language:** The hymns are written in Tamil, making it accessible to common people while promoting spiritual and cultural values.

• **Themes:** The hymns emphasize concepts like **surrender (sharanagati)**, divine grace, and the glory of Vishnu's avatars.

• **Festivals:** Many verses from the Divya Prabandham are recited during Vaishnavite festivals like **Vaikuntha Ekadashi** and temple processions.

questions.question: Which of the following is a Fundamental Duty mentioned in the Indian Constitution?

options.text: To vote in the Lok Sabha election
To educate child up to 18 years of age

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To protect the natural environment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• **Fundamental Duties** are enshrined in **Article 51A** of the Indian Constitution, added by the **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**.

• One of the Fundamental Duties explicitly states that it is the duty of every citizen of India **to protect and improve the natural environment**, including **forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife**, and to have compassion for living creatures.

• The inclusion of Fundamental Duties was inspired by the **Constitution of Russia (Soviet Union)** to inculcate a sense of responsibility among citizens toward the nation and society.

• While Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, they act as moral obligations for citizens to ensure active participation in nation-building.

• Protecting the environment is critical to addressing issues like **climate change**, **pollution**, and **loss of biodiversity**, thereby ensuring sustainable development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Other Fundamental Duties:**

• **To abide by the Constitution** and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag, and the National Anthem.

• **To cherish and follow the noble ideals** that inspired the national struggle for freedom.

• **To uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.**

• **To defend the country** and render national service when called upon to do so.

• **To value and preserve the rich heritage** of our composite culture.

• **Environmental Protection in India:**

• The **Environment Protection Act, 1986** is one of the key legislative frameworks to safeguard the environment.

• India is a signatory to international agreements such as the **Paris Agreement** under the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change.

• Various government initiatives like **National Green Tribunal** and **Clean India Mission** aim to enhance environmental sustainability.

• **Role of Citizens:**

• Active participation in tree plantation drives, waste management, and conservation of water resources.

• Promoting renewable energy usage and adopting eco-friendly practices in daily life.

• Awareness campaigns to educate people about the importance of protecting the environment.

• **Global Environmental Efforts:**

• The **United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC)** focuses on global climate action.

• The **Kyoto Protocol** and **Paris Agreement** aim to reduce greenhouse gas emissions globally.

• Organizations like the **World Wildlife Fund (WWF)** and **Greenpeace** work to protect biodiversity and mitigate environmental degradation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Constitutional Provisions:**

• **Article 48A:** The State shall endeavor to protect and improve the environment and safeguard forests and wildlife.

• **Article 51A(g):** It is the duty of every citizen to protect the natural environment, including forests, lakes, rivers, and wildlife, and to have compassion for living creatures.

• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976:**

• This amendment introduced the concept of Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution.

• It was enacted during the tenure of **Prime Minister Indira Gandhi**.

• **Environmental Challenges:**

• India faces issues like air pollution, deforestation, water scarcity, and waste management.

• Efforts are needed to balance economic development with environmental conservation.

</ul

questions.question: Which of the following amendment act of the Indian constitution made Sikkim a full-fledged State of the India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**36th Amendment Act, 1975**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__
 __ 
• The **36th Amendment Act of 1975** was responsible for making **Sikkim** a full-fledged state of India. 
• Before this amendment, Sikkim was recognized as an **associate state** of India under the provisions of the **35th Amendment Act, 1974**. 
• With the 36th Amendment Act, Sikkim was officially included as the **22nd state** of India. 
• The amendment added **Article 371F** to the Constitution of India to provide special provisions for Sikkim, considering its unique socio-political and cultural characteristics. 
• This amendment was essential to integrate Sikkim into the Indian Union and ensure its governance under the Indian Constitution. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Sikkim's Status Before 1975:** 
• Sikkim functioned as a **protectorate** under India since the treaty signed in **1950** between the Indian government and the Chogyal (monarch) of Sikkim. 
• It maintained a unique status and was governed by the Chogyal, with India handling its defense, external affairs, and communications. 
• **35th Amendment Act, 1974:** 
• This amendment introduced the concept of an **associate state** for Sikkim, a status that was unique in the Indian Constitution. 
• It provided limited representation for Sikkim in the Indian Parliament. 
• However, political instability and demands for full integration into India led to the passing of the 36th Amendment Act. 
• **Special Provisions Under Article 371F:** 
• Article 371F was incorporated to protect **customs, laws, and traditions** of Sikkim while ensuring its integration into India. 
• It allowed for special provisions regarding the composition of the Legislative Assembly of Sikkim. 
• It recognized the unique **rights of the Sikkimese people**, including their cultural and social heritage. 
• **Geographical Significance:** 
• Sikkim is located in the northeastern region of India and shares borders with **Bhutan, Nepal, and China (Tibet)**. 
• Its strategic location is crucial for India's defense and foreign relations in the Himalayan region. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Historical Context:** 
• Sikkim's merger with India was facilitated by a **referendum held in 1975**, where the majority of Sikkim's population voted for integration. 
• The Chogyal's rule was abolished following the referendum, and Sikkim's monarchy came to an end. 
• **Impact of the Amendment:** 
• Sikkim's inclusion in India as a state strengthened **India's territorial integrity**. 
• It ensured that Sikkim's residents enjoyed the rights and privileges of Indian citizens. 
• The state's unique identity and heritage were preserved through the special provisions under Article 371F. 
• **Examples of State Reorganization:** 
• Similar amendments have been made for other regions, such as the creation of **Telangana** in **2014**. 
• The Indian Constitution provides a framework for the reorganization of states through **Article 3**. </ul

questions.question: In which sport did Praveen Kumar Sobti won medals at the Asian Games?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Discus throw**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Praveen Kumar Sobti**, an Indian athlete, was renowned for his achievements in the **Discus throw** event. 
• He represented **India** in various international competitions, including the **Asian Games**. 
• Praveen Kumar Sobti won **two medals** in the Asian Games in the **Discus throw** category: 
• A **gold medal** at the **1966 Asian Games** held in Bangkok. 
• A **silver medal** at the **1970 Asian Games** held in Bangkok. 
• In addition to his success in the Asian Games, he also represented India in the **Olympics** in 1968 and 1972. 
• Praveen Kumar was not only an athlete but later became famous as an actor, particularly for his role as **Bheem** in the Indian television series **Mahabharat**. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 
• **Discus Throw:** 
• The **Discus throw** is a track and field event where an athlete throws a heavy disc called a **discus** to achieve the longest distance possible. 
• The sport has its roots in ancient Greece and was part of the original **Olympic Games**. 
• Athletes require a combination of **strength, technique, and agility** to excel in this sport. 
• The discus used in competitions typically weighs **2 kilograms** for men and **1 kilogram** for women. 
• **Asian Games:** 
• The **Asian Games**, also known as the **Asiad**, is a multi-sport event held every four years among athletes from all over Asia. 
• The first Asian Games were held in **1951** in **New Delhi, India**. 
• India has a strong history of participation in the Asian Games, winning medals in various sports such as athletics, wrestling, shooting, and hockey. 
• **Praveen Kumar Sobti’s Career:** 
• Born on **6 December 1947** in Punjab, India. 
• He joined the **Border Security Force (BSF)** at the age of 20 and pursued athletics while serving the nation. 
• Besides his medals in the Asian Games, he also secured **four medals** at the Commonwealth Games. 
• After retiring from sports, Praveen Kumar Sobti transitioned to **acting** and politics. 
• **Other Sports Options:** 
• **Long Jump:** Involves jumping as far as possible from a take-off point. Not related to Praveen Kumar Sobti. 
• **Shooting:** A sport involving precision and aiming skills. Praveen Kumar was not associated with this sport. 
• **Wrestling:** A combat sport involving grappling techniques. While India has a strong wrestling tradition, Praveen Kumar’s achievements were in discus throw.

questions.question: As of July 2025, who is the Chairperson of the Lok Sabha Estimates Committee?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sanjay Jaiswal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The **Chairperson of the Estimates Committee** in the Lok Sabha as of **July 2025** is **Sanjay Jaiswal**, a prominent Member of Parliament and a senior leader from the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

• The **Estimates Committee** is one of the three financial committees in the Indian Parliament, tasked with examining budgetary allocations and ensuring efficient use of public resources.

• The committee consists of **30 members**, all of whom are elected from the Lok Sabha (House of the People) based on proportional representation by means of a single transferable vote.

• The Chairperson of the committee is always chosen from the ruling party or alliance in the Lok Sabha to ensure effective coordination between the government and the committee.

• **Sanjay Jaiswal** has been actively involved in parliamentary proceedings and is known for his expertise in financial oversight and governance matters, making him a suitable choice for this role.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Estimates Committee Overview:**

• The Estimates Committee was first constituted in **1950** and is the largest parliamentary committee, consisting of 30 members.

• Its function is to scrutinize the **budget estimates** presented by the government to ensure that expenditure aligns with the principles of economy and efficiency.

• The committee also examines whether the expenditure is within the policy framework approved by Parliament.

• The committee does not question the policy but focuses on its implementation and financial implications.

• **Eligibility and Membership:**

• Only members of the **Lok Sabha** can be part of this committee. Members from the Rajya Sabha are not included.

• The Chairperson is usually a member of the ruling party or coalition, ensuring smooth communication with the executive branch.

• **Sanjay Jaiswal:**

• **Sanjay Jaiswal** is a senior BJP leader and a Member of Parliament from **Paschim Champaran constituency in Bihar**.

• He has been serving as an MP since **2009** and is known for his contributions to parliamentary debates and his leadership roles within the party.

• His experience and expertise in public administration and financial matters make him a trusted leader for overseeing the functioning of the Estimates Committee.

• **Important Functions of the Estimates Committee:**

• To suggest alternative policies for achieving the efficiency and economy in administration.

• To examine whether the money is well laid out within the limits of the policy implied in the estimates.

• To suggest the form in which the estimates shall be presented to Parliament to make them transparent and comprehensible.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Other Financial Committees:**

• The **Public Accounts Committee (PAC)** examines the accounts showing the appropriation of funds and ensures transparency in government spending.

• The **Committee on Public Undertakings (COPU)** reviews the working of public sector enterprises and evaluates their financial performance.

• **Relevance of the Estimates Committee:**

• This committee plays a crucial role in ensuring that government spending is in line with public welfare and economic development goals.

• It acts as a watchdog, holding the executive accountable for its financial decisions and implementation.

</ul

questions.question: In December 2024, the Union Health Minister said that the TB incidence rate in India has decline to __________ per 100000 population in 2023.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**195 per 100,000 population**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• In December 2024, the Union Health Minister announced that the **Tuberculosis (TB) incidence rate** in India had declined to **195 per 100,000 population** in 2023. 
• This decline reflects the success of the government’s initiatives under the **National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP)**. 
• The **World Health Organization (WHO)** had earlier estimated India's TB incidence rate for 2021 as **210 per 100,000 population**, showcasing a significant improvement in disease control efforts. 
• The reduction aligns with India’s commitment to achieve the **United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** and eliminate TB by **2025**, five years ahead of the global target. 
• Various initiatives like the **“Nikshay Poshan Yojana”** (nutritional support for TB patients) and the **introduction of new diagnostic tools** have contributed to this progress. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Tuberculosis (TB):** 
• **TB** is a contagious disease caused by the bacteria *Mycobacterium tuberculosis*. 
• It primarily affects the lungs but can also impact other parts of the body, such as the spine, brain, and kidneys. 
• The disease spreads through the air when people with active TB in their lungs cough, sneeze, or spit. 
• **National TB Elimination Programme (NTEP):** 
• Previously known as the Revised National Tuberculosis Control Programme (RNTCP), it was renamed in **2020** to reflect India’s commitment to eliminating TB. 
• NTEP aims to eliminate TB in India by **2025** through early diagnosis, treatment, and care for patients. 
• Key components include free diagnostic services, drug delivery, and nutritional support through the **Nikshay Poshan Yojana.** 
• **WHO Global TB Report:** 
• The **World Health Organization (WHO)** releases an annual Global TB Report to track progress in eliminating TB worldwide. 
• As per the 2022 report, India accounted for **26%** of the global TB burden, but significant strides have been made in reducing the incidence rate. 
• **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):** 
• The **SDG 3** aims to ensure healthy lives and promote well-being for all ages, including ending the epidemics of TB by **2030**. 
• India has advanced its target to eliminate TB by **2025**, showing strong political commitment and implementation of health programs. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Nikshay Poshan Yojana:** 
• Launched in **2018**, this scheme provides **₹500 per month** to TB patients for nutritional support during their treatment. 
• The funds are directly transferred to patients' bank accounts under the **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)** system. 
• **Advanced Diagnostic Tools for TB:** 
• India has adopted modern diagnostic techniques like **CB-NAAT (Cartridge-Based Nucleic Acid Amplification Test)** and **TrueNat** to detect TB and drug-resistant TB quickly and accurately. 
• These tools have improved early detection rates, helping to reduce TB transmission. 
• **Patient-Centric Care:** 
• Under the NTEP, patients receive **free access to TB drugs and treatment**, including for multi-drug resistant TB (MDR-TB). 
• Community engagement and awareness campaigns have been crucial in reducing the stigma associated with TB.

questions.question: World Poverty Clock Report is released by which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**World Data Lab**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **World Poverty Clock** is a tool developed by the **World Data Lab** to monitor progress against poverty reduction worldwide. 
• It was launched in **2017** and provides data on poverty in real time by estimating the number of people escaping poverty and those entering it. 
• The World Poverty Clock uses data from multiple credible sources, including **World Bank, UN, IMF, and national statistics agencies**. 
• Its key focus is on tracking progress towards achieving the **United Nations Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 1**, which aims to eradicate extreme poverty by **2030**. 
• The tool covers data from over **190 countries** and provides insights into poverty trends at both the global and regional levels. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **World Data Lab:** 
• **World Data Lab** is a social enterprise that specializes in building advanced data models and tools to measure global development challenges. 
• It provides forecasts and insights on key indicators such as **poverty, demographics, water security, and climate change**. 
• The organization is headquartered in **Vienna, Austria**, and collaborates with global institutions like the UN and World Bank. 
• The World Poverty Clock is one of its flagship projects, helping policymakers and researchers track poverty trends efficiently. 
• **World Bank:** 
• The **World Bank** is an international financial institution that provides loans and grants to countries for development projects. 
• It is focused on reducing poverty and promoting sustainable development worldwide. 
• The World Bank publishes key reports such as the **Global Economic Prospects** and **World Development Report** that include data on poverty. 
• While the World Bank is an important source of poverty data, it is not the creator of the World Poverty Clock. 
• **UNDP:** 
• The **United Nations Development Programme (UNDP)** is the UN's global development network, working to eradicate poverty and reduce inequalities worldwide. 
• UNDP monitors progress on the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** and assists countries in implementing policies to achieve these goals. 
• It provides poverty-related data but does not manage the World Poverty Clock. 
• **IMF:** 
• The **International Monetary Fund (IMF)** is an organization focused on global monetary cooperation, financial stability, and economic growth. 
• It publishes reports and provides data on macroeconomic indicators, including poverty levels. 
• The IMF contributes to global poverty data but is not directly involved with the World Poverty Clock. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Key Characteristics of the World Poverty Clock:** 
• It uses advanced data modeling techniques to estimate poverty levels in real-time. 
• The tool calculates the number of people escaping poverty per second and identifies regions lagging behind in poverty reduction. 
• It tracks poverty based on the **international poverty line** of living on less than **$1.90 per day**. 
• The World Poverty Clock is accessible online and is widely used by researchers, policymakers, and institutions. 
• **Connection to SDG 1:** 
• The World Poverty Clock aligns its data monitoring with **Sustainable Development Goal 1**, which focuses on eradicating poverty in all forms. 
• It provides actionable insights to help countries and organizations achieve the SDG targets by **2030**. </ul

questions.question: Who was India's first-ever gold medallist at the Asian Games?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sachin Nag**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sachin Nag** was India's first-ever gold medallist at the **Asian Games**.
 
• He achieved this feat in the inaugural Asian Games held in **1951** in **New Delhi, India**.
 
• Sachin Nag won the gold medal in the **100-meter freestyle swimming event**, marking a historic moment for Indian sports.
 
• The 1951 Asian Games were hosted by India and featured participants from multiple Asian countries, making it a significant event in the region's sports history.
 
• His victory was a proud achievement that highlighted India's emerging talent in international sports post-independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Asian Games (1951):**

 
 
• The **Asian Games** were held for the first time in **1951** in **New Delhi**, India.
 
• The event was inaugurated by then Prime Minister **Jawaharlal Nehru**.
 
• A total of **11 countries** participated in the games, competing in **57 events across 8 sports**.

questions.question:
The Aravalli Green wall Project covers which of the following state?

I. Delhi

II. Bihar
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• The **Aravalli Green Wall Project** aims to tackle environmental challenges like desertification, deforestation, and soil erosion by developing a green ecological corridor along the **Aravalli mountain range**.

• This project covers states that are part of or near the **Aravalli range**, which includes **Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan, and Gujarat**.

• **Delhi** lies at the northern end of the Aravalli range and is one of the regions included in this project to mitigate urban environmental stress. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***

• **Bihar**, however, is geographically located in eastern India and is not part of the Aravalli range. The state is not covered under the Aravalli Green Wall Project. ***Hence, statement II is incorrect.***

• The project aligns with India's commitment to combat **land degradation and desertification** under the **United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Aravalli Range:**

• The Aravalli range is one of the oldest mountain ranges in the world, stretching approximately **692 km** across parts of **Delhi, Haryana, Rajasthan, and Gujarat.**

• It acts as a natural barrier, preventing the expansion of the Thar Desert into the fertile plains of northern India.

• The range is home to diverse flora and fauna, including many endangered species, and plays a vital role in maintaining ecological balance.

• **Desertification in India:**

• India is one of the most vulnerable countries to desertification, with about **29.32% of its total geographical area** affected by land degradation as per the Desertification and Land Degradation Atlas of India (2016).

• States like Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Haryana are among the most affected due to their proximity to the Thar Desert.

• **United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD):**

• The UNCCD was established in **1994** to address desertification and promote sustainable land management.

• India is a signatory to the UNCCD and has pledged to achieve **land degradation neutrality by 2030** as part of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

• **Goals of the Aravalli Green Wall Project:**

• To increase forest cover and green areas along the Aravalli range.

• To improve groundwater recharge and ensure the conservation of biodiversity.

• To create sustainable livelihoods for local communities through eco-development initiatives.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Environmental Significance:**

• The Aravalli Green Wall Project aims to combat climate change by sequestering carbon and reducing urban heat island effects in areas like Delhi.

• It ensures protection against wind erosion and the spread of desertification from the Thar Desert into the fertile northern plains.

• **Policy Alignment:**

• The project aligns with India's **National Action Programme to Combat Desertification** (NAPCD), which was launched in **2001**.

• It also contributes to India's obligations under the **Paris Climate Agreement** to enhance forest cover and reduce carbon emissions.

• **Threats to Aravalli Range:**

• Unregulated mining, urbanization, and deforestation are significant threats to the Aravalli range.

• Efforts like the Green Wall Project aim to restore ecological balance and curb further degradation.

``

questions.question: Which Mauryan architectural structure is famous for its beautiful, sculpted gateways?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sanchi Stupa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__

• **Sanchi Stupa**, located in Madhya Pradesh, is one of the most renowned Buddhist monuments in India. It is famous for its beautifully sculpted gateways, known as **Toranas**.

• The gateways of the Sanchi Stupa are intricately carved and depict various **Buddhist symbols**, stories from Buddha's life, and Jataka tales that represent the moral and ethical teachings of Buddhism.

• The structure was commissioned by **Emperor Ashoka** in the 3rd century BCE during the Mauryan Empire and is considered one of the oldest stone structures in India.

• The central dome of the Sanchi Stupa symbolizes the **enlightenment** of the Buddha, while the gateways serve as a representation of the **four cardinal directions** and provide access to the circular pathway around the stupa.

• The Sanchi Stupa has been recognized as a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** since 1989 for its historical, cultural, and architectural significance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Features of Sanchi Stupa:**

• The stupa is a hemispherical dome with a central chamber that houses relics of the Buddha or other revered figures in Buddhism.

• The **Toranas** (gateways) are located in the four cardinal directions and are adorned with exquisite carvings depicting various events from the life of Buddha and his teachings.

• The circular path around the stupa, known as **Pradakshina Patha**, is meant for circumambulation, a sacred ritual in Buddhist practice.

• **Historical Background:**

• The Sanchi Stupa was commissioned by Emperor Ashoka in the 3rd century BCE and later expanded by the Shunga dynasty.

• It is a prominent example of Buddhist architecture and art during the Mauryan period.

• The stupas were used to house relics of the Buddha and serve as a place of meditation and devotion.

• **Other Options Explained:**

• **Amaravati Temple:** Located in Andhra Pradesh, this site is famous for its Buddhist stupas and sculptures but does not feature sculpted gateways like Sanchi Stupa.

• **Ajanta Caves:** Known for their rock-cut Buddhist caves and paintings, these caves are not associated with sculpted gateways.

• **Nalanda University:** An ancient center of learning in Bihar, it is renowned for its educational and architectural significance but does not have sculpted gateways like Sanchi Stupa.

• **Significance of Sanchi Stupa:**

• The stupa represents the **spread of Buddhism** in India during the Mauryan Empire.

• It serves as an important symbol of peace and enlightenment and is a major pilgrimage site for Buddhists worldwide.

• The intricate carvings on the gateways provide insights into the **artistic and cultural achievements** of the Mauryan and post-Mauryan periods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Restoration Efforts:** The Sanchi Stupa underwent restoration during the colonial period by British officers like Sir John Marshall, ensuring its preservation for future generations.

• **Symbolism of the Stupa:** The dome symbolizes the **cosmic mountain**, and its umbrella-like structure represents the **three jewels of Buddhism** (Buddha, Dharma, Sangha).

• **Inscriptions:** The Sanchi Stupa features inscriptions in the **Brahmi script**, which provide valuable historical insights.

• **Influence on Later Architecture:** The architectural style of the Sanchi Stupa influenced the design of other stupas and Buddhist monuments across Asia.

``

questions.question: In April 2025, who developed India's first genome edited rice varieties?

• **India’s first genome-edited rice varieties** were developed by the **Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR)** in **April 2025**.

• These rice varieties were developed using the **CRISPR-Cas9 genome-editing technology**, a cutting-edge tool for genetic modification.

• The genome-edited rice is aimed at improving **agronomic traits** such as higher yield, pest resistance, and environmental adaptability.

• This initiative is part of India’s larger efforts to enhance food security and reduce dependency on traditional breeding methods for crop improvement.

• The ICAR is an autonomous body under the **Department of Agricultural Research and Education (DARE), Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare**, Government of India, and has been at the forefront of agricultural innovation.

__

• **Genome Editing and CRISPR-Cas9 Technology:**

• **Genome editing** involves modifying the DNA of an organism to add, delete, or alter specific traits.

• **CRISPR-Cas9** is a revolutionary gene-editing technology that allows precise changes to the DNA sequence.

• This technology is faster, cheaper, and more accurate than traditional genetic engineering methods.

• It holds potential applications in agriculture, medicine, and biotechnology.

• **Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR):**

• ICAR was established on **16 July 1929**, headquartered in **New Delhi**.

• It is the apex body responsible for coordinating, guiding, and managing agricultural research and education in India.

• ICAR has contributed significantly to the **Green Revolution**, White Revolution, and now supports emerging technologies like genome editing.

• **Importance of Genome-Edited Crops:**

• They can address critical challenges like **climate change, pest resistance, and food security**.

• Genome-edited crops have the potential to reduce the use of chemical pesticides and fertilizers, making agriculture more sustainable.

• They play a significant role in enhancing the nutritional quality of staple crops.

• **Other Research Institutions Involved in Agriculture:**

• **International Rice Research Institute (IRRI):** Headquartered in the Philippines, it focuses on improving rice productivity and sustainability worldwide.

• **National Institute of Plant Genome Research (NIPGR):** Located in New Delhi, it specializes in genomics research for crop improvement.

• **Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI):** A premier institute under ICAR, known for its contributions to agricultural research and education in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **ICAR’s Achievements:**

• ICAR has developed numerous high-yielding and disease-resistant crop varieties.

• It was instrumental in the success of the **Green Revolution** in India.

• The organization also focuses on animal husbandry, fisheries, and soil health management.

• **Regulations for Genome Editing in India:**

• Genome-edited crops are regulated under the **Environment Protection Act, 1986**, and guidelines are provided by the **Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee (GEAC)**.

• ICAR collaborates with national and international bodies to ensure safe and effective use of genome-editing technologies.

questions.question: Who among the following established close relations with the French and modernized his army with their help?

__

• **Tipu Sultan**, also known as the "Tiger of Mysore," was a ruler of the Kingdom of Mysore in South India. He is known for his military innovations and resistance against British colonization.

• Tipu Sultan established **close relations with the French** as part of his strategy to counter British dominance in India. He sought French assistance in modernizing his army.

• He adopted **European military techniques** and utilized advanced weaponry, including the use of rockets, which were highly innovative for their time.

• Tipu Sultan's alliance with France was formalized through diplomatic missions. He even sent emissaries to **Napoleon Bonaparte**, seeking a joint effort to expel the British from India.

• He played a pivotal role in the **Anglo-Mysore Wars**, where his modernized army gave a tough challenge to the British forces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• He was a Maratha ruler and one of the key figures in the Maratha Confederacy during the 18th century.

• While he maintained relations with Europeans, his primary focus was on consolidating Maratha power rather than modernizing his army with foreign assistance.

• **Ali Wardi Khan:** 

• He was the Nawab of Bengal and is known for resisting Maratha incursions into Bengal during his reign.

• However, he did not establish close ties with the French or modernize his army with their help.

• **Shah Alam II:** 

• He was a Mughal Emperor who reigned during a period of decline for the Mughal Empire.

• He lacked the resources or influence to form alliances with European powers like the French for military modernization.

• **France-India Relations:** 

• During the 18th century, the French East India Company was active in India and sought to expand its influence, often allying with Indian rulers like Tipu Sultan.

• The French provided military training, troops, and equipment to Tipu Sultan in his fight against the British.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Anglo-Mysore Wars:** Tipu Sultan fought four Anglo-Mysore Wars, with the last one (1799) resulting in his death and the fall of Mysore to the British.

• **Military Innovations:** Tipu Sultan's army was among the first in the world to use iron-cased rockets, which were later adopted by the British.

• **Napoleon and Tipu:** Tipu Sultan's correspondence with Napoleon aimed at forming a coalition to drive out the British from India, but this alliance could not materialize fully.

• **Legacy:** Tipu Sultan is remembered as a visionary ruler who aimed to modernize his state and resist colonial domination.

questions.question: Which of the following article of the Indian constitution states that there shall be a Vice-President of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 63**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 63** of the **Indian Constitution** explicitly states that there shall be a **Vice-President of India**.
 
• The **Vice-President** is the second-highest constitutional office in India, following the President.
 
• The primary role of the Vice-President is to act as the **ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha** (Upper House of Parliament).
 
• If the office of the President becomes vacant due to death, resignation, removal, or otherwise, the Vice-President acts as the **acting President** until a new President is elected.
 
• The Vice-President is elected by the members of an **electoral college** consisting of both elected and nominated members of the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Eligibility Criteria for the Vice-President:**

 
 
• A candidate must be a **citizen of India**.
 
• The candidate must be at least **35 years old**.
 
• The candidate should not hold any office of profit under the Government of India or any state government.
 
 
 
• **Election Process:**
 
 
• The Vice-President is elected through a process of **proportional representation** using a **single transferable vote system**.
 
• The election is conducted by the **Election Commission of India**.
 
 
 
• **Term and Removal:**
 
 
• The Vice-President holds office for a term of **5 years**.
 
• He/she can be removed from office through a **resolution passed by the Rajya Sabha** and agreed to by the Lok Sabha.
 
 
 
• **Historical Facts:**
 
 
• The first Vice-President of India was **Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan**, who later became the President of India.
 
• The Vice-President can also act as the **Presiding Officer** in the absence of the Speaker of Lok Sabha, though this situation is rare.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Article 62:** Deals with the time frame for holding elections to fill a vacancy in the office of the President. It is **not related** to the Vice-President.
 
• **Article 68:** Deals with the election of the Vice-President but does not state the existence of the office. Hence, it is **incorrect**.
 
• **Article 65:** Provides provisions for the Vice-President acting as President during temporary vacancies. It does **not establish** the office of the Vice-President.
 
• **Article 63:** Clearly mentions that "There shall be a Vice-President of India," making it the **correct answer**.

questions.question: The biological catalysts which help in the breakdown of food in humans known as __________
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Enzymes**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 __ 
• **Enzymes** are biological catalysts that speed up chemical reactions in the body, including the breakdown of food into simpler molecules for absorption. 
• They are produced by various glands and organs in the digestive system, such as the salivary glands, stomach, pancreas, and intestines. 
• **Digestive enzymes** include amylase (breaks down carbohydrates), protease (breaks down proteins), and lipase (breaks down fats). 
• Enzymes work by lowering the activation energy required for biochemical reactions, making digestion faster and more efficient. 
• Without enzymes, the human body would struggle to convert complex food substances into absorbable nutrients, leading to nutrient deficiencies and other health issues. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Functions of Enzymes:** 
• **Amylase:** Found in saliva and pancreas; converts starch into simple sugars like maltose and glucose. 
• **Protease:** Found in stomach (pepsin), pancreas, and intestines; breaks down proteins into amino acids. 
• **Lipase:** Secreted by the pancreas; breaks down fats into fatty acids and glycerol. 
• **Lactase:** Found in the small intestine; breaks down lactose (milk sugar) into glucose and galactose. 
• **Role in Digestion:** 
• Enzymes enable the chemical breakdown of macronutrients (carbohydrates, proteins, and fats) into absorbable forms. 
• The process begins in the mouth with salivary enzymes, continues in the stomach with gastric juices, and completes in the intestines with pancreatic and intestinal enzymes. 
• Enzymes also facilitate nutrient absorption in the small intestine by converting food into smaller molecules that can pass through the intestinal wall. 
• **Other Options Explained:** 
• **Lymph:** A fluid in the lymphatic system that helps in immune responses and waste removal. It does not aid directly in digestion. 
• **Mucus:** A protective secretion that lubricates and protects the digestive tract lining but does not break down food. 
• **Bile:** A digestive fluid produced by the liver and stored in the gallbladder; it emulsifies fats but is not an enzyme. 
• **Interesting Facts:** 
• The human pancreas secretes approximately 1.5 liters of pancreatic fluid daily, rich in enzymes. 
• Enzymatic activity can be affected by factors such as pH, temperature, and the presence of inhibitors or activators. 
• Diseases like lactose intolerance occur due to enzyme deficiencies (e.g., lack of lactase). 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Enzyme Deficiencies:** Conditions like **pancreatic insufficiency** and **lactose intolerance** arise due to inadequate enzyme production. 
• **Temperature Sensitivity:** Enzymes function optimally at specific temperatures (around **37°C** in humans) and may denature at extreme temperatures. 
• **pH Levels:** Different enzymes work best at specific pH levels. For example, **pepsin** requires an acidic environment, while **amylase** functions in neutral to slightly alkaline conditions. 
• **Applications of Enzymes:** Beyond digestion, enzymes are used in industries like food processing, pharmaceuticals, and biofuel production. 
• **Research:** Ongoing studies aim to develop artificial enzymes for therapeutic and industrial applications.

questions.question: Which two languages flourished alongside Sanskrit in Vedic ancient India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pali and Prakrit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pali** and **Prakrit** were the two languages that flourished alongside **Sanskrit** in ancient India during the **Vedic and post-Vedic period**.
 
• **Pali** was primarily used in the **religious texts of Buddhism**. It is the language in which the **Tripitaka**, the sacred Buddhist scriptures, were composed.
 
• **Prakrit** refers to a collection of vernacular languages that were spoken by the common people. It was widely used in **Jain and Buddhist texts**.
 
• While **Sanskrit** was the language of the elite and intellectuals, **Pali** and **Prakrit** catered to the linguistic needs of the **common masses**, making religious and philosophical teachings more accessible.
 
• The adoption of **Pali** and **Prakrit** by religious leaders like the Buddha and Mahavira played a crucial role in **spreading their teachings** across diverse communities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pali Language:**

 
 
• **Pali** is closely associated with **Theravāda Buddhism**, and its scriptures are preserved in the **Pali Canon**, also known as the **Tipitaka**.
 
• It was a lingua franca in ancient India, especially in regions where Buddhism was prevalent.
 
• The language helped in the dissemination of **Buddha's teachings** to a larger audience, as it was simpler compared to Sanskrit.
 
 
 
• **Prakrit Language:**
 
 
• **Prakrit** refers to a group of closely related languages spoken in ancient India. It was the primary spoken language of the masses during the Vedic and post-Vedic periods.
 
• It was widely used in **Jain texts** like the **Agamas** and in **Buddhist literature**.
 
• Prominent types of Prakrit include **Magadhi Prakrit**, **Ardhamagadhi**, and **Sauraseni Prakrit**.
 
 
 
• **Sanskrit:**
 
 
• **Sanskrit** was the language of Vedic hymns, philosophical texts, and classical literature. It is considered the **root of many Indian languages**.
 
• Texts like the **Vedas**, **Upanishads**, **Mahabharata**, and **Ramayana** were composed in Sanskrit.
 
• Unlike Pali and Prakrit, Sanskrit was primarily used by scholars, priests, and the elite class.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Explained:**
 
 
• **Hindi and Urdu:** These languages developed much later, during the **medieval period**, and were heavily influenced by Persian and Arabic.
 
• **Bengali and Tamil:** These are regional languages that developed during the later periods of Indian history. Tamil, however, is part of the ancient Dravidian family, but it did not flourish alongside Sanskrit during the Vedic era.
 
• **English and Persian:** These languages became prominent in India during the **colonial and medieval periods**, respectively, and were not contemporaneous with Sanskrit in ancient India.
